title: Semantic page layout
summary: Describe the parts of a page with header, nav, main, section, article, aside and footer.

quiz.q: How many `<main>` elements should a page normally have?
quiz.explain: `main` marks the central content of the page, so there should be one visible `main` per page.

quiz.q: Which element is best for a single blog post that could be shared on its own?
quiz.explain: `article` is for self-contained content. `section` groups related content within a page.

quiz.q: Fill in the element for the group of main menu links.
Put these in the order they usually appear inside `body`.
quiz.explain: A common order is header, then navigation, the main content, an aside, and the footer at the end. Some pages put the aside inside main, but this order is the common one.

exercise.task:
Turn the content of `index.html` into a semantic layout.

- A `<header>` that is a direct child of `body` and contains the `<h1>`.
- A `<nav>` inside the header with at least 3 links.
- Exactly one `<main>`, containing at least 2 `<section>` elements.
- An `<article>` and an `<aside>` inside `main`.
- A `<footer>` that is a direct child of `body` and has some text.
hints: Sketch the outline: header, main, footer as three children of body.
nav goes inside header. section, article and aside go inside main. Each section should start with a heading.
